81.from: Day 10 Q47 — GIR to dextrose concentration

calc_items.title: Holliday–Segar maintenance
calc_items.question: A stable 16-kg child: calculate the routine 24-h maintenance volume using 100/50/20.
calc_items.working: 1000 + (16−10)×50 = 1300 mL/day. This is a starting estimate, not an automatic prescription in AKI.

calc_items.title: Urine-output staging
calc_items.question: A 15-kg child makes 54 mL of urine in 12 h. Calculate the urine output in mL/kg/h and the KDIGO urine-output stage.
calc_items.working: 54/(15×12) = 0.30 mL/kg/h. It is <0.5 for ≥12 h → stage 2; stage 3 requires <0.3 for ≥24 h or anuria ≥12 h.

calc_items.title: Fluid overload
calc_items.question: Weight was 12.0 kg before illness and is now 13.5 kg. Calculate the % fluid overload relative to baseline.

calc_items.title: GIR repair
calc_items.question: At 100 mL/kg/day, what dextrose percentage is required for a GIR of 7 mg/kg/min?

calc_items.title: D10 mass repair (CALC-D14-C6)
calc_items.question: For an 8-kg child, a hypothetical 5 mL/kg D10 bolus is ordered. Calculate the volume and the glucose mass separately.
calc_items.working: 8×5 = 40 mL. D10 = 10 g/100 mL = 0.1 g/mL; 40×0.1 = 4 g. Exercise only; actual hypoglycaemia treatment varies by clinical setting/protocol.

calc_items.title: Fractional excretion of sodium
calc_items.question: Urine Na 20 mmol/L, plasma Na 140 mmol/L, urine creatinine 50 mg/dL, plasma creatinine 2 mg/dL. Calculate the FeNa.

calc_items.title: Arterial oxygen content repair (CALC-D18-C3)
calc_items.question: Hb 15 g/dL, saturation 92%, ignoring dissolved O₂. Calculate the CaO₂.
calc_items.working: CaO₂ = 1.34×15×0.92 = 18.492 mL O₂/dL; saturation is 0.92, not 92.

calc_items.title: Guideline-specific hypertonic saline arithmetic
calc_items.question: Under NICE NG29, a 2.7% saline 2 mL/kg bolus is considered for acute symptomatic hyponatraemia. What volume for an 18-kg child (maximum 100 mL)?
calc_items.working: 2 mL/kg × 18 kg = 36 mL, below the 100-mL maximum. This is NICE-specific; local protocols may use 3% with different volumes.
